lines.text: Dark, empty gym. One bank of lights flickers on.
A man laces his worn shoes on a lone bench.
He chalks his hands. Dust hangs in the cold air.
He loads a barbell plate by plate, the clang echoing.
The bar leaves the floor. His jaw sets, veins rising.
Rep after rep. Sweat drips onto the rubber floor.
Beyond the window, the sky is still black.
He racks the bar and meets his own eyes in the mirror.
Nobody's watching. That's when it counts. Nobody but me.
He slides on more weight and goes again.
The window behind him turns pale gold as first light arrives.
The door opens. Early members arrive to find him already finishing.
He walks out past them, towel over his shoulder, unhurried.
